identity.title: Christopher Hitchens VS. William Dembski FULL
identity.dateBasis: Dembski’s own bibliography identifies this debate with Hitchens at Prestonwood Church, Plano, on 18 November 2010. The organizer archive independently lists the 2010 event Does a Good God Exist? and both speakers. External pages are used for identity only, never imported as extra debating evidence.
identity.speakerIdentityBasis: Named introductory biographies, moderator handoffs, long uninterrupted formal rounds, direct name-addressing and first-person references establish the two primary speakers. Mixed transition or cross-talk evidence still requires attribution review.

acquisition.method: YouTube public Innertube Android player captions; srv3 XML normalized locally

content.coverageNote: The English ASR track spans the entire recording. The sole gap over ten seconds is 16.4 seconds inside the opening edited montage before the live-event window. There is no such gap in the debate. The final rolling caption extends 1.520 seconds past the player duration; all events remain preserved. Live-event coverage begins at 1:27.079 and includes all primary formal rounds, audience answers and closing statements, followed by the excluded host closing.
content.captionCaution: The neutral motion is whether a good God exists. Dembski distinguishes design from Christian revelation, admits difficult theological tensions and independently develops an incarnation and forgiveness case. Hitchens distinguishes deism from theism and mere atheism from secular humanism; do not turn his concessions into advocacy of a designer or require atheism to entail one political system. Historical and scientific statements are participant claims, not verified external facts. Preserve ASR words in exact quotations; evident lexical or numeral transcription errors are not participant mistakes. Full source includes edited opening montage, institutional framing, logistics, audience-question prompts and closing prayer. Do not score third-party material. Frozen host exclusions and any dependent content are unavailable for credit or penalty. Ordinary audience-question prompts are context, not adopted third-party advocacy. Verify the complete source; if an unenumerated substantive host intervention, unique host argument, distinct side or material gap is found, return a source-gate failure before inventory selection. Below-high speaker attribution requires independent audio checking, not artificial confidence inflation.

excludedIntervals.speaker: Dan Panetti and Caleb (opening hosts)
excludedIntervals.summary: The opening hosts frame the event as preparation to engage atheists, compare worldview training to football practice, and endorse scripture and spiritual preparation for this life and the next. The whole continuous opening exchange is conservatively excluded.
excludedIntervals.burdenImpactRationale: This is Christian institutional framing, not an additional account of divine existence or goodness. Its scriptural authority and afterlife assumptions are independently defended by Dembski at 1:29:24–1:31:01 and 1:46:03–1:50:09. Neither primary speaker directly answers this pre-event exchange.

excludedIntervals.speaker: Event moderator (name not established)
excludedIntervals.summary: The moderator invites listeners to Prestonwood as a place to search for truth using scripture as a guide. The mixed transition into biographies is conservatively included.
excludedIntervals.burdenImpactRationale: The invitation supplies no independent motion argument and repeats the Christian scriptural framework Dembski independently adopts. It is excluded from both sides’ evidence, with no directly dependent primary response.

excludedIntervals.speaker: Event moderator (name not established)
excludedIntervals.summary: After both closing statements, the moderator recommends Probe Ministries and its resources for answering questions arising from the debate. The complete promotional passage is conservatively excluded.
excludedIntervals.burdenImpactRationale: This institutional recommendation supplies no substantive answer or unique argument for the motion. It adds no third position, occurs after the primary exchange ends, and receives no response from either debater.

excludedIntervals.speaker: Larry Taylor
excludedIntervals.summary: The school head recounts his preference for biblical truth over atheism and closes with a Christian prayer affirming God’s revelation, Christ’s sacrifice, and eternal life. This entire testimony and prayer is excluded.
excludedIntervals.burdenImpactRationale: Personal conviction, scriptural truth and salvation in Christ repeat Dembski’s independently stated conversion and incarnation case at 1:46:03–1:50:09 and forgiveness defense at 1:54:52–1:57:59. The closing prayer offers no additional public premise or unique motion argument and is not answered by either primary speaker.
